hub.note: The shared substrate: GLP-1RAs down-weight incentive salience through mesolimbic dopamine circuitry and central-amygdala GABA transmission. Because reward domains converge on that substrate, an effect tuned for food bleeds outward — but the bleed weakens with every step away from the metabolic core.

domains.label: Food
domains.synthesis: The proximate evolutionary target. Reduced motivational salience for high-energy palatable food is demonstrated across rodent operant work, human fMRI cue-reactivity, and the obesity indication itself — every evidence tier points the same way.

domains.label: Alcohol
domains.synthesis: The strongest cross-reward case outside food. Two human randomised trials (Hendershot 2025, SEMALCO 2026) show reduced consumption and craving, and the mechanism is not purely dopaminergic — central-amygdala GABA is implicated. Observational cohorts agree but inflate the effect.

domains.label: Nicotine
domains.synthesis: Moderate and mostly preclinical. Exendin-4 blunts nicotine-induced accumbal dopamine and place preference in rodents; the human signal is a secondary outcome — fewer cigarettes per day in the smoker subgroup of an alcohol trial — not a dedicated smoking RCT.

domains.label: Opioids
domains.synthesis: Preclinical only. Liraglutide reduces heroin self-administration and reinstatement in rats, and EHR cohorts report lower opioid-use outcomes — but no opioid-use-disorder trial has read out, and the observational effect size is implausibly large.

domains.label: Stimulants
domains.synthesis: Preclinical only, and mechanistically the weakest fit. Exendin-4 reduces cocaine self-administration in mice, but stimulant addiction is less coupled to metabolic and satiety signalling, and no human stimulant trial exists.

domains.label: Behavioural
domains.synthesis: Open. Reduced gambling, compulsive shopping, and nail-biting under GLP-1RAs appear only as case reports and clinician anecdote. A shared incentive-salience mechanism is assumed, not shown — and uncontrolled reports are the format most vulnerable to bias.

caution: Two failure modes this page exists to block. (1) Borrowing confidence across domains — the strong food and alcohol evidence does not transfer to opioids or gambling, which rest on preclinical models and uncontrolled reports. (2) Reading the observational halo as pharmacology — EHR cohorts report roughly 85% lower substance-use outcomes, an effect size too large to be drug action alone and heavy with confounding by indication. The EVOKE cognitive-trial failure is the standing reminder that observational neuropsychiatric signals can evaporate under randomisation.
